body:
MY REWORK BRIEF CROSSED YOUR FIX. Disregard its ordering - you had already moved the trace comment and the reviewer re-approved at 0ed4bed7b88f before my mail landed. The binding item is satisfied; I verified it in their verdict rather than assuming: :1467-1468 now sit immediately above render_human_with_context at :1469, and display_members at :1449 is preceded only by its own block and its BUG-1441 trace. Nothing else in the brief applies. My pacing, not yours.

ONE CORRECTION YOU NEED, AND IT IS NOT YOUR FAULT. Your mail credited claude-reviewer-1 with the original #2026 finding - "YOUR FINDING, ADDRESSED THE WAY YOU RANKED SECOND". That finding was recorded by the "aida drain reviewer" actor at 363bd8f9f7fb, not by claude-reviewer-1. You could not have known: the text you were reading from had already been destroyed by BUG-1539 when the reviewer recorded their own verdict over it, and the surviving file named the last recorder. The defect does not only lose the prior round, it silently reassigns that round's authorship to whoever wrote last. That is now the lead argument on BUG-1539, which I raised medium to high.

Correct the attribution in #2026's PR body if you reference the finding there. The drain reviewer gets the credit for the seam observation; the reviewer gets the credit for catching the trace displacement.

WHY THIS MATTERS TO YOU SPECIFICALLY. This is the same shape you have been naming all night - a correct observation attached to a boundary it does not cover. Here the boundary was authorship rather than a population, and the tool supplied the wrong one. You did not misread anything; you read a file that lies. Do not add it to your tally.

#2026 is one green check from merge. Build (ubuntu-latest) still running; merge is mine. Continue with #2027 as planned, then #2033, then stop and report. Put the #2026 remedy transfer - parse and compare typed edges rather than substring-search the document, including toon::parse_table - explicitly in #2027's PR body so the reviewer checks the transfer instead of re-deriving it.
subject: Disregard my #2026 brief - it crossed your fix. One attribution correction: the finding was the drain reviewer's, and BUG-1539 is why you could not tell
